messages:
zara: quickstart weirdness — local CLI prints 'first call OK' but our CI that hits the sample Ruby app gets a 302 -> billing checkout and then the test HTTP client follows it and stores HTML snapshot. workspace created with invite, no card on file. anyone seen the Ruby snippet behave differently? :confused:

miguel: ruby net/http defaults to following redirects if you use some helpers; can you paste the request?

zara: minimal repro (curl):
```
$ curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-ruby' https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Accept: */*
> Authorization: Bearer sk-test-ruby
\n< HTTP/1.1 302 Found
< Location: https://console.redwood-inference.example/billing/checkout?reason=onboard
< Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
```

zara: CLI quickstart prints 200 earlier so dev copy thinks it's good. Ruby quickstart doesn't set Accept header explicitly.

katie: ah — parity issue. TS/Python SDKs set `Accept: application/json` and get 402 JSON; our Ruby quickstart uses bare Net::HTTP and ends up with `*/*` which the gateway treats as browser-like and redirects.

miguel: temporary workaround: add `req['Accept'] = 'application/json'` in the Ruby example or configure your CI HTTP client to not follow redirects. That makes the gateway return `HTTP/1.1 402` with JSON `{"error":{"code":"billing_required","message":"Add billing to enable first calls"}}`.

zara: one more wrinkle: our internal HTTP retry middleware was treating 302 as retryable and retried the POST to the streaming transcription endpoint, which double-submitted an upload and caused duplicate processing in a customer's integration test. that's scary.

katie: yes we need to treat 3xx as terminal for non-idempotent methods. also for streaming endpoints prefer returning an `event: error` SSE payload instead of redirecting.

sdk-bot: logged DEVEX-7021 (update Ruby quickstart to set Accept header and note billing gating) and INF-7022 (gateway: return machine-readable 402 for API clients; make 3xx terminal for POST/PUT/PATCH; SSE endpoints emit error event).

prod-deploy-bot: canary INF-7022 deployed to dev cluster at 3525007785 :rocket:

miguel: confirmed on canary: adding `Accept: application/json` to the Ruby sample returns `HTTP/1.1 402` + JSON and CI tests can assert billing-gate. updated the sample readme and added CI note about redirect handling. leaving thread, will follow DEVEX-7021 for the PR. :thumbsup:
